Name: Android Binder IPC Deserialization RCE
Synopsis: The remote Android device is vulnerable to a remote code execution vulnerability via Binder IPC.
Description: The remote Android device exposes an unprotected IPC (Inter-Process Communication) endpoint. By sending a specially crafted serialized `Parcelable` object via an Intent, an unauthenticated attacker can trigger a type confusion vulnerability in the `readSerializable()` method, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the targeted application.
Solution: Restrict access to exported IPC components by setting `android:exported="false"` in the `AndroidManifest.xml` or implement strict signature-based permissions. Avoid using unsafe deserialization methods.
Plugin Output: The following exported components were detected:\n- com.example.app.VictimReceiver\n- com.example.app.PaymentService

Name: Android App AllowBackup Enabled
Synopsis: The Android application has the allowBackup flag enabled.
Description: The Android application has the `android:allowBackup` attribute set to true in its manifest file. This allows anyone with adb access to backup the application data, potentially exposing sensitive information such as session tokens or databases.
Plugin Output: Backup extraction successful via adb backup command.

Name: Cleartext Traffic Permitted
Synopsis: The Android application allows cleartext network traffic.
Description: The application network security configuration permits cleartext (HTTP) traffic. This could allow an attacker to intercept or modify network communications.
Solution: Configure the network security configuration file to set `cleartextTrafficPermitted="false"` for all domains.
